name: Jev 1.14
contract: Choice, Score and Noul as in Jev 1.13, plus a fourth question type, Box, that returns the four edges of a single bounding box in an image and needs Jev 1.14; Choice and Score return probabilities and a 0 to 1 confidence, and Noul returns a probability of yes without a separate confidence
limits: API model ID jev-1.14.0 (jev-latest and jev-preview now resolve to it); 64k tokens per request and 32k per question, as for Jev 1.13, and 262k for both with the long-context header; request body at most 32 MiB; rate limits set per organization; the vendor intends 60 days of warning before jev-1.13.0 is formally deprecated and 30 days before jev-1.14.0
price: 0.042 USD per million input tokens ($42 per billion), output free, unchanged from Jev 1.13
evidence: Vendor documentation says the model was trained with RLCD to return calibrated decisions, in the same words as for Jev 1.13. Leaderboard results, not graded studies: Decision Index 0.4.1 Full score 60.2 (an accuracy index, with calibration on a separate tab) and edgeevals.ai v0.2 clinical-decision accuracy 76.8 (rank 7=)
disclosure: Vendor pages accessed 2026-10-28. The models table lists text input for both Jev versions, while the images page says both accept images behind the TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images header, and the launch post says jev-1.13.0 was multimodal all along

name: Microsoft-Decision-1
contract: Noul, Choice and Score through a Decision API type; a text or JSON state plus one or more typed questions; also rubric-based grading, and abstention expressed as an extra answer option such as cannot tell
limits: text only; inputs up to 32K tokens in the Foundry catalog; deployment types DataZoneStandard in selected regions and GlobalStandard; the blog and the Learn page state no context or rate limit; catalog lifecycle Preview
price: 0.042 USD per million input tokens, output free
evidence: Vendor-reported: highest accuracy in its 36-benchmark comparison of nearly 150,000 questions; third on calibration, 1.5 behind Jev 1.13.0 and 0.9 behind Quyet-1.0-Large; 1.3% of decisions change on average over eight perturbations. The Learn page cautions that scores are not absolute calibrated ratings. A leaderboard result, not a graded study: edgeevals.ai v0.2 clinical-decision accuracy 78.1 (rank 6=)
disclosure: Model version 1, post-trained from Qwen3.5-9B; API only, through Microsoft Foundry and OpenRouter; the blog says it will soon be rebased on other models

name: Trio-Spark
contract: Choice questions only, with 2 to 8 choices; returns the selected choice, a probability for each choice and a confidence equal to the probability of the selected choice, with a decide, review or abstain disposition; v1.3 of 2026-10-15 is the current release and adds visual input
limits: 1,024 expanded input tokens including task, state, choices and any visual input; 65,536-byte request body in the v1.0 text API; at most 16 questions per request; recommended model ID trio-spark-v1.3 (older aliases route to the current model and do not pin historical weights)
price: 0.042 USD per million billed input tokens, output free; 100 free decisions for a new account
evidence: Vendor-reported only: expected calibration error 0.019 on its own 2,977-decision text panel (10 bins); the vendor states that calibration on this panel does not guarantee calibrated confidence in a different application, and that its accuracy table is developer-run and not independently certified
disclosure: Submitted by the publisher (issue #2). The model card is for a commercial API; weights and training code are not distributed. The former v1.0 card is merged into the current card, and Trio-Spark-DI is a separate research checkpoint, not the hosted model

name: Clef and Clef-Flash
contract: Noul, Choice and Score (types noul, choice and score) over text, JSON, images and video frames; Clef-Flash is a 9B multimodal model, and its card says the API is fully compatible with Jev and SystemOne
limits: the launch post states a 64k context window for Clef, against 32k for Jev; the Clef-Flash code defaults to 16,384 tokens; hosted on Workers AI
price: no price found on the launch post
evidence: Vendor: trained with label-smoothed cross-entropy plus a Brier loss to refine calibration; the Clef-Flash card has no calibration claim and reports a vendor internal accuracy run of Decision Index 0.2.1. Leaderboard results, not graded studies: edgeevals.ai v0.2 clinical-decision accuracy 74.8 (Clef 27B, rank 8=) and 66.7 (Clef-Flash, rank 20=); Decision Index 0.4.1 Full score 54.9 (clef) and 44.4 (clef-flash)
disclosure: Open weights under Apache-2.0 on Hugging Face, with Clef-Flash post-trained from Qwen3.5-9B (card created 2026-09-30), and hosted on Workers AI

name: pplx-decider v1.1 (27B)
contract: Choice in the card's usage example, and Choice and Noul decisions in the training pipeline of v1; images are supported
limits: 8,192 tokens for the text and all images of a decision; about 49 GiB of weights; no hosted API in the sources
evidence: Vendor: the supplied predict applies a saved calibration temperature. The card's accuracy claim, a Decision Index score rising from 56.4 to 61.56, is on an older edition and is not a calibration result. Both leaderboards list v1.2 rather than v1.1: Decision Index 0.4.1 Full score 68.0 and edgeevals.ai v0.2 clinical-decision accuracy 83.8 (rank 3)
disclosure: Open weights under Apache-2.0, base model Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B; the card calls the repository private, while the Hugging Face API showed it public and ungated on 2026-10-28
